A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ELEMENTAL, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting direct comparison. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v3 includes Appendices A-C. This difference is confirmed by inspection, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: v1 reports original IsaacGym benchmark experiments, component ablations, Ant generalization experiments, reward correlations, and code-execution measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports seed-aggregated generalization results and a Humanoid case study in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The three-phase procedure remains VLM feature generation, Approximate MaxEnt-IRL with PPO and gradient/weight normalization, and feature-count-based self-reflection. Algorithm 1 is unchanged. The appended prompts and worked example disclose implementation details without establishing an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine IsaacGym tasks and the same Ant scenarios: original, reversed observations, lighter gravity, and backward running. The new Humanoid case study examines an existing task rather than extending coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1-3 retain the same comparators and ablation variants. The normalization, text-demonstration, and random-visual-demonstration rows already appear in v1; v3 expands their descriptions and renames the normalization rows without adding comparison methods.

E3.justification: Both retain GPT-4o, five RL-generated demonstrations per task, final-100-step evaluation, and the same Ant modifications. Newly specified hyperparameters, expert keyframe selection, and text-demonstration sampling document existing experiments rather than establish protocol revisions. Appendix C traces the retained procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a Humanoid case study tracing two rounds of feature generation, feedback, rescaling, and introduction of a lateral-velocity feature. This provides a limited new examination of self-reflection. The systematic ablations and generalization tests were already present in v1.

E5.justification: v3 Table 5 newly reports means and standard deviations across three seeds for the Ant generalization comparisons. Both versions already disclose three seeds and retain best-seed results in the main tables. The addition does not establish more runs or introduce significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 retain their numerical results. New Table 5 supplies seed-aggregated results, including original-Ant performance of 6.80±1.17 for ELEMENTAL and 4.44±2.45 for EUREKA. Appendix C.2 adds Humanoid feature values, learned weights, and episode-length outcomes across iterations.

T1.justification: The linear reward formulation, MaxEnt likelihood, feature-expectation gradient approximation, and normalization equations retain their mathematical substance. Equations are renumbered and the linear reward formula moves inline; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: combining visual demonstrations and VLMs with IRL and iterative self-reflection. The headline claims of 42.3% better benchmark performance and 41.3% better generalization remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 expands interpretations of the existing normalization, textual-input, and random-demonstration ablations. Its limitations section develops demonstration-quality dependence and possible runtime remedies, while Appendix C.2 discusses nonlinear feature expressiveness and inspectability. These extend v1's existing discussion without changing its central interpretation.

D1.justification: v1 refers to supplementary prompts and hyperparameters but does not include them in the supplied PDF. v3 Appendices A-B provide actual prompts, TorchScript interface requirements, grid-search disclosure, learning rate, IRL iterations, policy-training steps, code-sampling counts, and network architecture. These substantially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to EUREKA, Peng et al. (2024b), and other language-model-assisted robotics methods are retained. Reference-style changes, shortened venue descriptions, and related-work copyediting do not introduce new research positioning.

P1.justification: Most of the main narrative and section sequence remain intact. v3 tightens prose, expands explanations of existing ablations, separates limitations from the conclusion, and adds an Impact Statement and appendices. Author and conference-header text also change.

P2.justification: The paper is substantially reformatted from a single-column layout to a two-column main text, with resized and relocated figures, tables, and algorithm display. v3 also adds hyperparameter and uncertainty tables and boxed prompts and case-study outputs. The original figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: Appendices A-C address a substantial reproducibility gap: v1 promises supplementary material but omits the actual prompts and key training settings, whereas v3 supplies them and a worked execution trace. Table 5 also makes generalization variability across seeds inspectable. These additions substantially improve the paper's transparency and assessability, although the main claims still rely on unchanged best-seed summaries and uncertainty reporting remains limited.
